articles.title: UCF vs Baylor: Knights Grounded 41-9 on Space Game Night
articles.matchup: Final: Baylor (5-3) 41, UCF (4-4) 9, Fri., Oct. 30, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando. Next: at Kansas, Sat., Nov. 7, David Booth Kansas Memorial Stadium, Lawrence
articles.text:
Baylor 41, UCF 9. Friday was the annual Space Game at Acrisure Bounce House, the night we honor where this university came from: a school built to send talent to Kennedy Space Center and the space program in the 1960s. The alumni tailgate had a 4 Rivers buffet, aliens and robots. The band's halftime show was Space Mission X. Everything was ready for liftoff except, sadly, the offense. Houston, we have a problem, and it wore green and gold.

Six days after the Homecoming double-overtime thriller over BYU, the Bears got rolling early. Keyone Jenkins was intercepted in the first quarter, Baylor turned it into a touchdown, and the hole kept getting deeper. Down 20-6 at halftime turned into 34-6 in the third quarter after DJ Lagway hit two touchdown throws in under two minutes. Baylor rolled up 503 yards.

We had our sparks. Will Stone was perfect, 3 of 3, and his 57-yarder as the first half expired made the whole Bounce House jump. Josh Derry took a short throw from Alonza Barnett III and turned it into a 67-yard rocket down to the Baylor 8. Rocco Marriott broke a 56-yard run in the final minute. Jahleel Culbreath made nine tackles and a sack, Ty Bartrum added nine stops, and Horace Lockett and Tackett Curtis each got home to the quarterback too.

Here is the honest debrief, because Knights fans do not hide from the film. We went 2 of 15 on third down and 0 for 3 on fourth down. We ran 30 times for 66 yards. Two late trips inside the Baylor 10 ended with no points: a fourth-and-1 stop at the Baylor 5 and a fumble at the 7 on the final play. Our quarterbacks were sacked seven times. Mission control will be up late.

We are 4-4 and 2-3 in the Big 12, and the work is not done. The defense held Baylor to 20 points in the first half and kept fighting to the final snap. Next up is a trip to Lawrence to face Kansas on Nov. 7. Charge On, and keep looking up.

Baylor can have this one. We still have the rockets, the robots and the best halftime show in the Big 12.

articles.title: Baylor vs UCF: DJ Lagway, Bears Roll 41-9 at the Space Game
articles.matchup: Final: Baylor (5-3) 41, UCF (4-4) 9, Fri., Oct. 30, Acrisure Bounce House, Orlando. Next: vs. Iowa State, Sat., Nov. 7, McLane Stadium, Waco
articles.text:
Baylor 41, UCF 9. Back in Waco on Friday night, students wrapped up the third and final night of Fright Night on the Moody side of Fountain Mall, with carnival games, food trucks and a sorority banner contest. The haunted house was fine, y'all, but the real fright was halfway across the country at Acrisure Bounce House, where the Baylor Bears crashed UCF's annual Space Game and sent the Knights' launch straight back to the hangar.

After back-to-back losses to TCU and Kansas, this team needed a night like this, and DJ Lagway delivered it. He completed 16 of 25 throws for 319 yards and four touchdowns with zero interceptions. Two went to Tony Livingston, a 4-yarder in the first quarter and a 21-yarder in the third. Then Gavin Freeman ran under one deep down the middle for 77 yards and a score, and it was 34-6 before the Knights could find the countdown clock. Matthew Klopfenstein caught the last one from 5 yards out early in the fourth.

Freeman finished with five catches for 114 yards. Jadon Porter turned two grabs into 74 yards, including a 53-yard catch-and-run that set up a field goal late in the half. Ryelan Morris ran 11 times for 82 yards, and Caden Knighten punched one in from 2 yards. Rhett Armstrong hit from 45 and 29 in the final two minutes of the second quarter, and we went to the break up 20-6.

But brag on the defense first at the next tailgate. UCF finished 2 of 15 on third down and 0 for 3 on fourth down, and the Knights managed 66 rushing yards on 30 carries. Our guys were credited with seven sacks. Devon Jordan intercepted Keyone Jenkins in the first quarter, which set up the opening score. LeVar Thornton Jr. broke up two fourth-down throws. Traevon Mitchell stuffed a fourth-and-1 at our 5 late, and on the very last play Michael Allen fell on a fumble at our 7. Not one touchdown allowed. Not one.

Honest film session: 12 penalties for 85 yards is way too many, and Armstrong's 50-yarder before the end of the third quarter missed. We will clean that up. Zero turnovers, 503 yards and a road win in Orlando make the cleanup a lot more fun.

We are 5-3 and 3-2 in the Big 12. Iowa State comes to McLane Stadium on Nov. 7. Sic 'em, Bears.

articles.title: Charlotte vs Tulane: 49ers Fall 38-31 in Overtime Heartbreaker
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane (4-4) 38, Charlotte (1-7) 31 (OT), Fri., Oct. 30, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte. Next: at UAB, Sat., Nov. 7, 3:30 PM ET, Protective Stadium, Birmingham
articles.text:
Tulane 38, Charlotte 31, in overtime. Friday was the Military Appreciation Game at Jerry Richardson Stadium, with our military community and the UNC Charlotte ROTC cadets recognized, and the rest of us told to wear Niner green or our Halloween costumes. There was a Trunk-or-Treat in the tailgate lots before kickoff. For three and a half quarters, the 49ers handed out the best treat of all. Then the clock turned into a ghost story.

First, the good stuff, and there was a lot of it. Coming off the open week and the win at Temple, this team played like it believed. Khamani Alexander broke a 44-yard touchdown run. Aiden Bui hit from 48. Conner Harrell threw touchdowns to Jaden Barnes and Derrick Eley before halftime, and we went to the locker room up 24-14. Harrell finished 23 of 36 for 239 yards with two scores and no interceptions. Henry Rutledge ran 22 times for 121 yards and caught four balls for 79 more.

The defense showed up too. Jameel Croft Jr. intercepted Trace Johnson in the second quarter, Gavin Willis made 12 tackles, and Chase Usher and Kadin Schmitz each added eight. We had zero turnovers all night and held the ball for 33:47. Eley's 1-yard run with 10:52 left made it 31-21.

Here is where it hurts. Up 31-24 with 1:52 to go, we went for it on fourth down from the Tulane 42 and came up short. Tulane went 61 yards in 1:42, Johnnie Daniels broke a 33-yard run, and Johnson found Cameron Roberts with 10 seconds left to tie it 31-31. TJ Smith's 95-yard kickoff return in the second quarter already stung. That drive stung worse.

In overtime, Tulane scored first. We answered with first-and-goal at the 4 after a roughing flag, then got stuffed at the 3, and two throws to Barnes got knocked away. That was the night.

We are 1-7 and 1-3 in the American, but this was not the same team from September. Keep the green handy for Birmingham. UAB is next on Nov. 7 at Protective Stadium, and the Niners are close.

articles.title: Tulane vs Charlotte: Green Wave Rally to Win 38-31 in Overtime
articles.matchup: Final: Tulane (4-4) 38, Charlotte (1-7) 31 (OT), Fri., Oct. 30, Jerry Richardson Stadium, Charlotte. Next: vs. Tulsa (Homecoming), Sat., Nov. 7, 12:00 PM ET, Yulman Stadium, New Orleans
articles.text:
Tulane 38, Charlotte 31, in overtime. Back Uptown on Friday night, the Lavin-Bernick Center set up a free Halloween-eve horror movie night in the Rat. Fine idea, but the scariest show of the night was on ESPN2, live from Jerry Richardson Stadium, and this one had a happy ending for the Green Wave.

Let me be honest about the first three acts, because we have watched enough film to know a rough plot when we see one. Charlotte led 24-14 at halftime. Conner Harrell threw two touchdowns before the break, Henry Rutledge ran 22 times for 121 yards, and the 49ers held the ball for 33:47 without a single turnover. When Derrick Eley punched in a 1-yard run with 10:52 left, it was 31-21, and I was ready to hide behind the couch.

Then Trace Johnson grew up in about 11 minutes. He finished 28 of 36 for 284 yards, and he was surgical when it mattered. Johnnie Daniels ran 13 times for 99 yards and two scores, and Cooper Helmke's 27-yard field goal made it a one-score game. Up 31-24 with 1:52 left, Charlotte went for it on fourth down at our 42. Garrett Mmahat knocked the ball loose, it squirted out of bounds short of the sticks, and we had it back.

What came next goes in the scrapbook. Daniels ripped off 33 yards up the middle on third down, Johnson ran for a first down at the 11, and with 10 seconds left he found Cameron Roberts in the end zone. Helmke's kick tied it at 31-31.

In overtime, Destyn Hill caught two throws to set it up, and Dagan Bruno plowed in from a yard out. Then Charlotte got first-and-goal at our 4, and the defense stood up four straight times. TJ Smith broke up one throw to Jaden Barnes, and E'zaiah Shine knocked away the last one. Game over.

TJ Smith also returned a kickoff 95 yards for a touchdown in the second quarter, the kind of play kids will dress up as next Halloween. Dickson Agu made 14 tackles, and Kevin Adams III added 10.

We are 4-4 and 2-2 in the American, and after last week's loss to UTSA at Yulman, this bounce-back felt like a second wind off the river. Homecoming is next, with Tulsa coming to Yulman Stadium on Nov. 7. Roll Wave.
